description: Head-to-head questions: the twelve of the 2026-09-19 baseline (docs/plans/beating-closed-book.md §2) plus five written from the subject to fill the classes. Classes: held (the corpus certainly holds it), edge (the named work holds it, past what was ingested), broad (synthesis, evaluation), multi_part, how_to.

items.question: What is the most tangible proof for God for a modern atheist?
What will happen at the moment of death?
Will we have bodies in the beatific vision?
What is natural law and how do we come to know it?
Why does Aquinas say God is simple, and what is the strongest objection to that?
Who was the most impactful king during this period and why?
What does the genetic evidence say about how many Anglo-Saxons actually migrated to Britain?
Was the Anglo-Saxon arrival an invasion or a gradual migration?
Why do bees swarm, and how do I stop my hive from swarming?
How do I get a colony through its first winter?
What is a perfect syllogism and why did Aristotle care about the distinction?
What is the square of opposition?
What can the soul know once it is separated from the body?
When is a war just, according to Aquinas?
How did the separate Anglo-Saxon kingdoms come to be unified into England?
How do I check my hive for varroa mites and decide whether to treat?
How does Aristotle's modal syllogistic differ from his assertoric syllogistic, and why do scholars think it is flawed?
